# OmniNode

> OmniNode lets you hand coding-agent work to a model you choose: a model you run on your own machine or network, or a provider you pay for on your own API key. The model call goes from your machine to that model directly and never passes through OmniNode. Every run leaves a receipt naming the model that answered, and a meter prices each run against a baseline model. OmniNode does not sell inference.

State as of 2026-10-17. Shipped today, from public MIT-licensed packages on PyPI (omnibase-core, omnibase-infra, omnimarket) and with no OmniNode account: the local install of the `onex` command, `onex delegate`, a receipt for every run, `onex metering` against a baseline model, the local `onex dashboard`, and the Claude Code plugin `onex@omninode-tools`. In beta: invited outside users exercise that same delegation path from the same public quickstart. Not yet open: the hosted service, which is not open to outside users and which nothing on the shipped path needs.

This repository is OmniNode's public documentation. The one-page overview is the canonical statement of what ships; when another page disagrees with it, the other page is out of date.

## Start here

- [What OmniNode is, and where it stands](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/what-is-omninode.md): the one-page overview of what ships today, what is in beta and what is not yet open
- [Delegation quickstart](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/onex-plugin-quickstart.md): install `onex`, run a first delegation on your own model or key, read the receipt, meter the cost and add the Claude Code plugin, in about 15 minutes
- [Supported platforms](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/supported-platforms.md): where the `onex` tool installs, and how on each kind of computer
- [Repository README](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/README.md): what this repository holds and how it is organized

## How delegation works

- [Delegation dispatch](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/architecture/delegation-dispatch.md): how a delegation request travels from the command to a model and back
- [Delegation routing contract](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/architecture/delegation-routing-contract.md): how the model for a run is chosen from the backends you declared
- [Connecting to the cloud](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/connecting-to-the-cloud.md): the current state of the hosted service, and whose model credential a hosted run uses

## The platform underneath

- [Repository map and runtime concepts](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/architecture/repository-map-and-runtime-concepts.md): what each public repository owns and the runtime concepts that tie them into one system
- [Doctrine](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/doctrine/README.md): the stable principles the platform is built on
- [Building on the ONEX runtime](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/getting-started-local.md): write and run your own nodes locally, with no broker, database server or account
- [Self-hosting the full stack](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/guides/getting-started-self-hosted.md): run the broker, database and runtime services on your own infrastructure
- [Decision records](https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base/blob/main/adrs/README.md): the architecture decision ledger
